summary: H.J. Res. 213 is a joint resolution that uses the Congressional Review Act to disapprove and nullify a specific rule issued by the Environmental Protection Agency. The rule in question granted partial authorization to the California Air Resources Board to enforce its Commercial Harbor Craft regulations.

affected_groups.effect: Loses the partial authorization previously granted by the Environmental Protection Agency to enforce specific amendments to commercial harbor craft regulations.
Relieved from the specific new emission standards, compliance dates, and expanded vessel coverage authorized by the nullified rule.
affected_groups.group: Commercial harbor craft operators and vessel owners in California

key_provisions: Disapproves of the Environmental Protection Agency rule titled California State Nonroad Engine Pollution Control Standards; Commercial Harbor Craft Regulations; Notice of Decision.
Declares that the specified rule shall have no force or effect.
Revokes the partial authorization granted to the California Air Resources Board to amend its Commercial Harbor Craft regulation.

summary_detail.plain_summary: H.J. Res. 213 is a joint resolution that uses the Congressional Review Act to disapprove and nullify a specific rule issued by the Environmental Protection Agency. The rule in question granted partial authorization to the California Air Resources Board to enforce its Commercial Harbor Craft regulations.
summary_detail.significance: The resolution invalidates a federal agency's decision that allowed California to enforce stricter emission standards and regulations for commercial harbor craft, stopping the implementation of those specific rules under federal law.
